topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the scope of the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate pathogen recognition and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue injury by recognizing PAMPs and DAMPs using germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor functions and downstream signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the localization, ligand specificity, and intracellular signaling mechanisms of Toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic PRRs and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine intracellular sensing mechanisms and the assembly of the inflammasome complex to mature pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tissue sentinel cells detect danger, direct the extravasation of circulating leukocytes, facilitate lymphatic drainage, and can trigger severe systemic outcomes like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the active and passive mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive tissue healing, and lead to chronic inflammation or granuloma formation when unresolved.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the topic of the following lecture.
